true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate `downsize` definitions silently override each other

The file now defines `OptimizedImage.downsize` twice: once at line 145 with signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and again at line 149 with `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby does not support overloading; the second definition silently replaces the first. Any existing caller that passes width and height as separate arguments (the original 4-argument API, e.g. `downsize(from, to, 800, 600)`) will now raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (4 for 2..3)`. The overload must be removed or the signatures unified (e.g. accept *args and dispatch).

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Hardcoded 10MB client-side limit ignores per-type site settings

`validateUploadedFile` previously enforced `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (different limits for images vs attachments); it now hardcodes 10MB for both. If an admin configures `max_attachment_size_kb` above or below 10MB, or `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB, the client-side validation no longer matches the server: users may be wrongly blocked from uploading valid files, or allowed to select files the server will reject — and the 413 error handler at line 246 also reports the hardcoded 10MB rather than the actual configured limit, producing misleading error messages.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Animated GIFs are destroyed or fail downsizing

`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` routes animated GIFs (when `allow_animation` is true) to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` producing `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%` — gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects geometry like `WxH`, not a percentage, so the command fails and the GIF is never reduced (and the loop retries the same failing command 5 times). When `allow_animation` is false, `downsize_instructions` uses `#{from}[0]`, which silently strips all but the first frame, turning users' animated GIFs into static images. Additionally the animated-vs-static decision keys off `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but the tempfile path (e.g. `discourse-upload-image...`) has no `.gif` extension, so animated handling never actually triggers. Note also that the `from` and `to` paths are identical, so `convert` reads and overwrites the same file each iteration with compounding quality loss.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
API URL downloads now hardcode 10MB instead of the configured image size

`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. Sites that set `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB (e.g. 15MB) will now have API-based URL image downloads truncated/rejected at 10MB even though the subsequent downsize step could have brought them under the limit, and sites with a limit below 10MB now download more data than configured. The download cap should stay tied to the setting (or a named constant larger than any supported limit).

Downsize loop never breaks on failure and uploads oversized file anyway

In `create_upload`, the `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...` loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` but ignores its return value. If `convert` fails (returns false) or the image simply cannot be shrunk below the limit within 5 iterations, the code falls through and calls `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized (or unchanged) tempfile anyway, retrying an identical failing operation up to 5 times and wasting CPU. If downsizing fails or the file is still over the limit after the attempts, the upload should be rejected with a clear error instead of proceeding.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation calls sub! on possibly-nil host

The `before_validation` callback does `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` unconditionally. If a record is saved without a host (or the admin client sends a blank value — the DB column is null: false but validation happens first), `self.host` is nil and `sub!` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if self.host` (and rely on a presence/format validation to report the error).

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update/destroy raise NoMethodError for nonexistent host instead of 404

`update` and `destroy` look up the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call `host.destroy` / `host.save` without a nil check. A request for a missing or stale id (e.g. a row deleted in another tab) returns a 500 NoMethodError instead of a 404. Use `find` or raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record is nil.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host comparison is not case-insensitive on the input side

`record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but never downcases the `host` extracted from the URI, while the `before_validation` that stores records never downcases either (the format validation is case-insensitive). A stored host entered as `Example.COM` matches, but an incoming referer `HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM/path` yields `uri.host == "EXAMPLE.COM"`, which won't equal `lower(stored)`. Downcase both the stored value and the lookup value to make matching reliably case-insensitive.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are inserted raw, without the normalization the new model applies

The old `embeddable_hosts` setting explicitly accepted values like `http://eviltrout.com` (the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped `http(s)://` before comparing, and the removed specs confirm that format worked). The migration copies each line verbatim into the new table via raw SQL, bypassing the model's `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path. After migration, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `URI(referer).host` (e.g. `eviltrout.com`) against the stored value `http://eviltrout.com` with `lower(host) = ?`, which never matches — embedding silently stops working for those hosts. The migration should normalize each value (strip scheme/path) before inserting.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files

`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the `:category` fabricators. The contents were pasted into the wrong files. Fabrication happens to load every file in the directory so specs still pass, but the misnamed files will confuse future edits and any tooling that maps fabricator names to files — swap the contents back.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent

The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. On any site that never set the `embed_category` site setting (it defaulted to blank), the query returns zero rows, so `[0]` is nil and calling `['id']` on nil raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The same fragility exists on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`. This will block upgrades for sites that used embeddable_hosts but never picked an embed category. Guard with `.first`/`&.` and a fallback.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

false_positives.candidate:
Embedded *_ids hydration can produce undefined entries

In `_hydrateEmbedded`, for plural `*_ids` keys the code maps ids through `_lookupSubType`, which returns `undefined` when the id isn't present in the root payload, and then assigns the array to the plural property (the `hydrated || []` fallback never triggers since `map` always returns an array). Any payload whose `foo_ids` references an id not included in the sideloaded collection yields an array containing `undefined`, which will crash consumers doing `array[0].get('id')`. Filter out undefined values before assigning.

No uniqueness validation or DB index on host

Nothing prevents two EmbeddableHost rows for the same host (with different categories), and there is no index on `host`. Duplicates make `record_for_host`'s `.first` nondeterministic — a host could resolve to either category for imported topics — and every embed check (`host_allowed?` runs on every embedded comments request) does a full table scan. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` and a unique (or at least plain) index on `host` in the migration.

category_id is mass-assigned from params without existence check

`host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` accepts any integer. An invalid id is only silently replaced with the uncategorized category when blank, not when pointing to a nonexistent category, leaving an orphaned foreign key; the admin UI will then break when rendering the host's category. Validate that the category exists (e.g. `validates :category, presence: true` with a foreign-key constraint) before saving.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row

In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil — a user can receive a notification email (e.g. via a category watch or a mention) without ever having a topic_users row. The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, producing a NoMethodError and a 500 for exactly the users most likely to click an unsubscribe link. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` or handle the nil case by creating the record.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate: Unsubscribe mutates state via a GET request The new `unsubscribe` action is exposed via GET (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb) and immediately writes to topic_users (setting regular/muted). GET links in emails are followed by mail-client prefetchers, link scanners, and antivirus proxies, so a user's notification state can be changed without any intentional action; it also makes the endpoint CSRF-able via a simple tag for logged-in users. The GET should render a confirmation page that performs the change via POST, as the client-side unsubscribe template suggests was intended.

Unsubscribe sets notification_level directly, losing reason/changed-at bookkeeping and MessageBus notification

The action assigns `tu.notification_level` and saves the model directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`. That bypasses setting `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` and skips the MessageBus `notification_level_change` publish, so any other open browser tabs of the user will keep showing the old notification state for the topic until reload, and analytics/auditing of why the level changed is lost.

topicUnsubscribe client route is shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear

The `topicUnsubscribe` route (path `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`) is declared after the `topic` resource, whose child route `fromParamsNear` has path `/:nearPost`. Ember matches routes in declaration order, so `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe` matches `topic.fromParamsNear` with nearPost="unsubscribe" before the new route is ever reached. The unsubscribe page will instead load the normal topic route and attempt to treat "unsubscribe" as a post number. The route needs to be declared before the topic resource or nested so it wins.

unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url but most callers don't provide it

The `unsubscribe_link` text now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and `Email::MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part` call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. Only `send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`; any other email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` and no `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send. The interpolation should be conditional on the URL being present (or all callers updated and a test added for the missing-arg case).

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked check is skipped whenever any other email error exists

The BlockedEmail.should_block? call is guarded by `record.errors[attribute].blank?`, and each User.save with a changed email runs this validator. The intent is fine, but note that should_block? has a side effect (incrementing match_count and last_match_at) — because it runs inside model validation, any save of a user whose email changed (including admin edits, seed scripts, etc.) mutates these statistics, while genuinely blocked attempts that also fail format validation are never counted. If the stats are meant to record blocked signup attempts specifically, the counting should happen at the controller/signup path rather than inside a model validator.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked email match is case-sensitive and unnormalized, so it is trivially bypassed

BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact string lookup (`BlockedEmail.where(email: email)`) against the raw email entered on the signup form. The rest of the codebase normalizes email via Email.downcase (which lowercases and strips dots/plus tags for gmail-style providers) before storing/comparing, but this lookup does not. A blocked address like bad@spammer.com can be evaded simply by signing up as Bad@Spammer.com, or with gmail dot/plus variants (b.ad+1@gmail.com). Since the entire purpose of the feature is to keep blocked users out, the lookup should normalize the incoming email the same way User emails are normalized, and the blocked_emails rows should be stored normalized.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Origin check uses substring matching instead of strict origin comparison

`if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any message whose origin appears anywhere inside discourseUrl. This is a fragile check: for example if discourseUrl lacks a trailing slash, an origin like 'https://discourse.example.com' matches even when discourseUrl is 'https://discourse.example.com.evil.tld'-style misconfigurations, and it also matches when the configured URL merely contains the origin as a substring (e.g. discourseUrl '//example.com/path' vs origin 'https://example.com' — inverted cases aside, substring matching is not an origin comparison). Parse both URLs and compare scheme/host/port strictly before resizing the iframe based on a message.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage targetOrigin uses the full referer URL including path, which browsers reject

`parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the entire referer URL as the targetOrigin. Per the postMessage spec, targetOrigin must be only scheme://host[:port]; if it contains a path the browser throws a SecurityError (or silently fails in older browsers) and the message is never delivered. Since every real referer includes a path, the 'discourse-resize' message that app/assets/javascripts/embed.js relies on to size the iframe will never arrive, leaving the iframe at its default height. The referer should be reduced to its origin before being used as targetOrigin.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embedding authorization relies solely on the Referer header host

`ensure_embeddable` grants framing based only on `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Direct loads (no referer) are rejected, but referer is client-supplied and can be forged by non-browser clients, and any page on the allowed host — including user-generated content on that host — can embed arbitrary `embed_url` parameters, each enqueueing a retrieve job. The 60s redis throttle in TopicRetriever mitigates volume, but the only thing binding the embed URL to the page is this header check; consider also validating that the embed_url's host matches and documenting that the referer check is not a strong security boundary.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
PollFeed crashes on feed items without content

`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `.scrub` on `i.content` without checking for nil. Many Atom/RSS items only provide a summary/description and no content element, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil and the scheduled job raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire poll (and with retry disabled, nothing is imported until the next run). Guard with something like `(i.content || i.summary || '').scrub`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
TopicEmbed.create! runs even when PostCreator failed to persist the post

`creator.create` returns `@post` even when post creation rolled back (e.g. validation or host-spam rollback leaves @post set but not persisted, and in the spam case create swallows the rollback). `post.present?` is then true, so `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: post.topic_id, post_id: post.id)` runs with `post_id = nil` against a `null: false` column (and a possibly nil/unsaved topic_id), raising ActiveRecord::NotNullViolation out of the import path instead of cleanly skipping. Check `post.persisted? && post.errors.blank?` before creating the TopicEmbed.

absolutize_urls misses relative URLs that don't start with '/'

Only href/src values starting with '/' are rewritten. Relative links like `href="page2.html"` or `src="images/pic.png"` are left untouched, so in imported topics they resolve relative to the forum's domain and produce broken links/images. Use URI.join(url, href) (or equivalent) for any non-absolute URL instead of only root-relative ones.

raw_html cook method renders un-sanitized HTML into posts, enabling stored XSS

The new `cook_method == :raw_html` path returns `raw` verbatim, completely bypassing the PrettyText/Sanitize pipeline. Feed/import content is user-controlled HTML from an external source (PollFeed does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no sanitization, and TopicEmbed.import_remote passes Readability output straight through). `scrub` only fixes invalid byte sequences, it does not strip `<script>` or event handlers. The resulting post is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb (and anywhere else cooked posts render on the forum domain), so any script in a feed item executes in the forum's origin for every viewer, including logged-in admins. The imported content must be sanitized before being stored/served.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Dead .valign-helper rule left behind after flexbox conversion

The .contents block was converted from float/inline-block vertical-centering to flexbox with align-items: center, which makes the .valign-helper element (an inline-block 100%-height shim used to vertically center siblings) unnecessary. The rule remains in the stylesheet; if the corresponding span is also still emitted in the markup it will now participate as an extra zero-width flex item. The leftover markup/CSS should be removed as part of this change.

Float-based layout in .small-action breaks once it becomes a flex container

.small-action is now a flexbox container (@include flexbox()), but its children still rely on floats: .topic-avatar has float: left and the button has float: right. Floats are ignored on flex items, so the action button that previously sat at the far right of the row will now render inline immediately after .small-action-desc instead of being right-aligned. The .small-action-desc also lost its 'padding-left: 4em' which previously cleared the 45px-wide avatar; combined with the removed 'margin-top: 5px' and 'padding-top: 4px' this changes vertical alignment of the description text. Either convert the children to proper flex layout (e.g. margin-left: auto on the button) or keep the floats and don't make the container a flexbox.

align-items mixin emits invalid value for legacy -webkit-box syntax when 'baseline' is used

The new align-items mixin passes the value straight through to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align. The old 2009 flexbox syntax (-webkit-box-align) only accepts start/end/center/baseline/stretch — actually 'baseline' is not valid for -webkit-box-align in old WebKit (it accepts start, end, center, stretch only). .badge-wrapper.bullet calls @include align-items(baseline), so on browsers using the legacy -webkit-box syntax the alignment declaration is invalid and dropped, silently changing rendering there. If legacy support matters (which the prefixes imply), the mixin should map values per-syntax.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the `?` suffix so AMS never calls it

ActiveModelSerializers 0.8/0.9 (used by Discourse) only honors filter methods named `include_<attribute>?`. The method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never invoked and `website_name` is always serialized — including when `website` is blank, in which case `website_name` returns nil and clients see an explicit `website_name: null`. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

false_positives.candidate:
Second-level-domain comparison treats unrelated subdomains as the same site

The branch comparing `website_host.split('.')[1..-1] == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]` treats e.g. website `www.wordpress.com` and instance `forum.wordpress.com` (or any two customers of a shared hosting domain) as the same site and exposes the full URL path. The old behavior only showed the host; this change reveals path information for domains that merely share a suffix. Consider using an exact-suffix check (`website_host == discourse_host || website_host.ends_with?('.' + discourse_host) || discourse_host.ends_with?('.' + website_host)`) instead of comparing truncated labels, which also mishandles multi-part TLDs like `example.co.uk`.

website_name leaks the website domain for TL0 users seen by anonymous visitors

The `untrusted_attributes` list hides `website` (and other profile fields) from anonymous viewers of trust-level-0 users, but the new `website_name` attribute was not added to that list and has no `restrict_user_fields?` guard. As a result, an anonymous crawler can still read the domain (or full host+path) of a TL0 user's website via `website_name` even though `website` itself is suppressed, defeating the purpose of the restriction. Add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or gate its inclusion on `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

website_name returns nil for URLs without a scheme

`URI(website.to_s).host` returns nil for scheme-less websites like `example.com/user` (which Discourse accepts and displays). The method then returns nil even though `website` is present, so the profile shows no website name at all for those users. Previously the client-side `website.split("/")[2]` had similar limitations, but the new server-side code should normalize the URL (e.g. prepend `http://` when no scheme) before parsing instead of silently returning nil.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Light-theme color for embedded-post metadata link changed from 30% to 70% lightness

In the diff for .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a, the old rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 70%, so on light themes this link becomes much lighter than before — dark-light-choose is supposed to preserve the existing light value and only add the dark variant. This looks like a copy/paste of the complementary values into the wrong branch and will visibly regress light themes.

true_positives.golden_comment: This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness

In desktop/user.scss the .group-member-info .name rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 30% to 50%, unintentionally lightening group member names on light themes (the mobile version of the same rule in mobile/user.scss has the same change). The light branch should have preserved the original 30%.

true_positives.matched_candidate:

true_positives.golden_comment: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Member routes pass :id but controller requires :group_id, breaking add/remove member

The new routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are declared inside `resources :groups` without a `collection` block, so Rails treats them as member routes: the URL is `/admin/groups/:id/members` and the group id arrives as `params[:id]`. However both `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member` do `params.require(:group_id)`, which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (HTTP 400) for every real request. The JavaScript in `discourse/models/group.js` calls `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json`, matching the member route, so adding or removing a member from the admin UI will always fail. The specs pass because they invoke the controller actions directly with `group_id:` and never exercise the routing. Either wrap the routes in `collection do ... end` (so the client sends `group_id` as a query/body param) or change the controller to use `params[:id]`, and add a request/route-level test.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

false_positives.candidate:
Remove-member link is shown for automatic groups because `automatic` is resolved on the member

The item view's context is the member (a User), so `{{#unless automatic}}` looks up `automatic` on the user object, which never has that property — the condition is always true and the remove (×) link is rendered even when viewing an automatic group. The server rejects the removal with a 422, but the admin UI offers an action that can never succeed, and the failed call is silently unhandled (no error callback on `removeMember` in the model). Use `{{#unless view.parentView.automatic}}` (or pass the flag into the view) so the link is hidden for automatic groups.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
FallbackLocaleList#[] raises NoMethodError when SiteSetting.default_locale is blank

`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `.to_sym` on `SiteSetting.default_locale` before the `compact` runs. If the setting is ever nil or unset (fresh install, broken settings table, early boot before seeding), every translation lookup that goes through the fallbacks backend will raise NoMethodError. Guard with `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` (or only add it when present). Also note `locale` may be a String while the other entries are Symbols, so `uniq` will not deduplicate e.g. 'en' vs :en — harmless but wasteful; normalize to symbols.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests; background jobs and mailers will emit 'translation missing'

The translate accelerator only loads the YAML files for `config.locale` on demand (see `translate`, which calls `load_locale(config.locale)` only). The new fallback mechanism relies on `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` to load the fallback locales (site default locale and `:en`), but that is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any `I18n.t` call that happens outside a web request — Sidekiq jobs, digest/notification emails, rake tasks — with a locale whose translation only exists in the fallback locale (e.g. `:en`) will not have the fallback locale's files loaded, so the lookup returns a 'translation missing' string instead of falling back correctly. The fallback loading should happen inside the backend/translate path (or a central `with_locale`/`ensure_loaded!` hook) rather than only in the controller before_filter.

No tests for fallback ordering or lazy loading of fallback locales

This PR introduces custom fallback behavior (user locale → site default locale → :en) and a new `ensure_loaded!` code path, but adds no specs. Given that the lazy locale loader (translate_accelerator) and the fallbacks interact in non-obvious ways (e.g. fallback locale files must be explicitly loaded or lookups return 'translation missing'), a regression test covering a key that exists only in :en being resolved for a request in another locale — plus the background-job path — would catch the most likely failure modes.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Call to no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match any declared method

`UsernameForm.authenticate` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only declaration added by this PR is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in `UsernamePasswordForm`. There is no no-arg overload in any changed file, so this does not compile. Presumably the intent was `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` (or a passkeys-enabled check without the user requirement, since at this point `context.getUser()` is known non-null, making the `user != null` check in the helper trivially true).

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are never offered on a fresh (unauthenticated) login

The new helper `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Both call sites that replaced the old logic (`authenticate()` line 115 and `challenge(context, error, field)` line 137) previously filled the WebAuthn conditional-UI form data when the user was NOT yet set (`context.getUser() == null`) — that is the normal first-login case where passkey autofill (conditional UI) must be offered so the user can sign in with a discoverable credential. With the new condition, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` only runs when a user is already set in the context (re-authentication), so on a fresh login the `webauth` form / challenge attributes are never rendered and users can no longer log in with passkeys at all. This is exactly the scenario covered by the updated tests asserting `//form[@id='webauth']` is present on the initial login page, which would now fail. The condition should allow the fresh-login case (user == null) as well as the re-authentication case, e.g. by not requiring `user != null` here.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative cursor offsets are passed into queryset slicing, which Django rejects

The comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', but Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing: queryset[-5:95] raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'). Cursor offsets come from the client-supplied cursor string (`value:offset:is_prev`), which Cursor.from_string parses with int() and no validation, so any user with the optimized_pagination flag can send a negative offset and get a 500. The 'advanced feature' is non-functional and only adds a new error path.

true_positives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError before the optimized branch

`enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences organization_context.member unconditionally for non-superusers. Requests authenticated without an organization membership context (e.g., certain token-based or org-auth-token flows that ControlSiloOrganizationEndpoint permits) have member=None, so this raises AttributeError and 500s the endpoint even though the user was never going to use the optimized path. Guard with `organization_context.member is not None and ...` or getattr.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate by datetime; it crashes on the first page

The audit log endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on the attribute value, which is a Python datetime object. math.floor/datetime raises TypeError (an integer is required). get_item_key is invoked by build_cursor on every result set (via _build_next_values/_build_prev_values), so the very first request using ?optimized_pagination=true will 500. This paginator needs the same epoch-milliseconds conversion DateTimePaginator performs (strftime('%s.%f') * multiplier).

false_negatives.golden_comment: Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
BasePaginator silently clamps negative forward-cursor offsets instead of rejecting them

The change to BasePaginator.get_result replaces `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` with `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. A negative offset on a forward cursor previously raised a clear error; it is now silently treated as 0, so a client repeating a malformed/rewound cursor gets the first page again, which can cause infinite loops in polling consumers that keep following next cursors. Additionally, for is_prev cursors the raw (possibly negative) offset is still used in slicing and in the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check, making that boundary check inconsistent with the clamped slice in the non-prev path.

No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized audit log path

The PR adds ~100 lines of new pagination logic plus a new endpoint branch gated by query param and permissions, but no tests. Basic coverage (first page, next/prev cursor round trip, negative offset handling, non-privileged user requesting optimized_pagination, datetime ordering) would have immediately caught the math.floor(datetime) crash and the negative-slicing ValueError.

value_from_cursor returns a raw integer that is compared against a datetime column

Even ignoring the crash, OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged (an integer), and build_queryset injects it into `WHERE <table>.datetime <= %s`. For a datetime-ordered queryset the cursor value must be converted back to a datetime (as DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor does with fromtimestamp(value/1000)); comparing a datetime column to an integer epoch value will either error at the database level or silently match nothing/everything depending on coercion, corrupting pagination results.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative-offset "advanced feature" crashes: Django does not support negative slicing

When `enable_advanced_features` is true and a caller supplies a cursor with a negative offset (possible now because `Cursor.from_string` happily parses a negative offset from the `value:offset:is_prev` string), the code does `queryset[cursor.offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django's ORM does not support negative indexing — `QuerySet.__getitem__` raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false, so instead of crashing this will surface as a 500 for any user-supplied cursor with a negative offset. There is also no validation anywhere that a client-supplied cursor offset is non-negative, which is a security/robustness regression on a public API endpoint.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
BasePaginator change silently drops negative offsets for forward cursors, but still passes them for prev cursors

The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` alters `BasePaginator` behavior for all existing paginators: for forward cursors a negative offset is now silently clamped to 0, while for `is_prev` cursors a negative offset is still passed straight into the queryset slice, where Django raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`. Since client-supplied cursor strings are parsed into arbitrary integer offsets (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative values), a crafted or corrupted prev-cursor (`...: -5:1`) will now crash any endpoint using `BasePaginator`/`DateTimePaginator`/`Paginator`, not just the new optimized path. The offset should be validated/clamped in both branches.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot sort by datetime; endpoint 500s

The audit log endpoint now routes requests with `optimized_pagination=true` to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 838) is copied from the numeric `Paginator` and calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on the key. For `AuditLogEntry.datetime` that value is a `datetime`, so `math.floor` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`. Any request that passes `optimized_pagination=true` (and satisfies the admin check) will fail with a 500 as soon as `build_cursor` computes cursor keys. The previous code path used `DateTimePaginator`, which converts datetimes to timestamps.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

false_positives.candidate:
Module docstring still describes the buffer as sets, not sorted sets

The module docstring (and the glossary at line 58, "span-buf:s:* -- the actual set keys, containing span payloads") still describes the segment store as Redis sets and describes step 3 as adding payloads to a "set". After this change the keys are sorted sets scored by `end_timestamp_precise`, and the redirect/merge logic in add-buffer.lua uses ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN. The stale documentation will mislead anyone reasoning about ordering, eviction, or the max-segment-size behavior.

New hard 1000-span eviction silently drops spans, possibly including the root span

The script now evicts with `zpopmin` whenever a set exceeds 1000 members. ZPOPMIN removes the lowest-scored members (earliest `end_timestamp_precise`), which may include the segment's root span — evicting it does not clear the `span-buf:hrs:` flag, so the segment will still be treated as having a root but will flush without one, producing an incomplete segment. Additionally, evicted spans are dropped permanently with no metric, log, or outcome emitted, so data loss from oversized segments is invisible. The old behavior flushed oversized segments intact and only skipped them (with an error log and `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric) when reading — that check was removed in buffer.py without a replacement, so `max_segment_spans` is now a dead constructor parameter and the only guard against huge segments is this silent truncation.

Redirect resolution depth reduced from 10000 to 1000 without handling the truncated case

The redirect-following loop limit was lowered from 10000 to 1000. When the redirect chain exceeds 1000 hops, the loop simply ends with `set_span_id` pointing at an intermediate node rather than the true set root. The script then does `hset main_redirect_key span_id set_span_id` and merges the span into whatever set that intermediate id resolves to, so a very deep segment tree gets split into two segments that are never rejoined (the old comment explicitly documented this failure mode at depth 10k). There is no metric, error, or fallback when the limit is hit, making the split silent. If the reduction was intentional for latency, the depth-limit-exceeded case should at least be observable.

Unrelated, undocumented audit-log endpoint behavior change in a spans-buffer PR

This PR (titled/described as a spans buffer optimization) adds a new query parameter `optimized_pagination` to the audit log endpoint that switches pagination behavior based on a client-controlled flag, gated only on `is_superuser` or `member.has_global_access`. Aside from being broken (see OptimizedCursorPaginator datetime issue), it changes a public API contract with no tests, no changelog, and no relationship to the PR's stated purpose. It should be split out or removed.

true_positives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sample-rate helper swallows errors, drops valid rate 0, and runs for every stored event

_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps dict .get() chains in bare try/except Exception (which cannot raise for the normal case but will silently mask real problems), and uses `if client_sample_rate:` so a legitimate client_sample_rate of 0 is ignored. More importantly, it is invoked unconditionally in Factories.store_event for every event stored in every test, mutating normalized_data['sample_rate'] globally — a hidden side effect that can change event processing behavior in unrelated tests that happen to include an error_sampling context. Consider gating it and using explicit None checks instead of truthiness and broad excepts.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache key built with Python hash() is unstable and collision-prone

The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Python's hash() is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so every web worker computes a different key for the same project set, making the 60-second cache largely ineffective across the fleet and causing cache entries to be orphaned. Worse, hash collisions between two different project sets would cause one set's eligibility decision to be applied to the other, flipping upsampling on/off incorrectly. Use a deterministic key such as a comma-joined sorted id list or a hash from hashlib.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling eligibility checked against outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset

Inside _get_event_stats, the eligibility check passes the closure variable `dataset` rather than the `scoped_dataset` argument that is actually queried. In the dashboard-widget discover-split path, scoped_dataset is `discover` (with an errors-only query) while the outer dataset may be metrics_performance/metrics_enhanced_performance, so the transform decision is made for the wrong dataset: the errors split query never gets upsampled, and conversely a transformation decision valid for the outer dataset could be applied to a different scoped dataset. Pass scoped_dataset to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidental git submodule added at repo root

The PR adds a new git submodule `sentry-repo` pinned to the base commit a5d2909. This appears to be an accidental artifact of a local checkout (the PR description even says "Test 3"), and if merged it would add a nested copy of the repository as a submodule, breaking clean clones and confusing CI/tooling. It should be removed from the PR.

Eligibility cache has no isolation; tests and allowlist changes observe stale results

The 60s cache keyed by (org, project set) is never invalidated when the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes (invalidate_upsampling_cache exists but nothing calls it), so flipping the allowlist takes up to 60s to take effect with no code path wiring the invalidation. Additionally, tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py runs multiple tests against the same org+project set with different mocked allowlists; the first test's cached True result can leak into later tests (e.g. the partial-allowlist test expecting count==1 would get the upsampled 10) if the cache is not cleared between tests, making the suite order-dependent. Tests should clear the cache in setUp, and the option-change path should call the invalidation hook.

Empty project list returns False, disabling upsampling for org-wide queries

_are_all_projects_error_upsampled returns False when project_ids is empty. Queries that target all projects in an organization (no explicit project filter) can legitimately have project_ids resolved before this call, but if snuba_params.project_ids is ever empty for an org-wide query the upsampling silently never applies with no indication why. Worth confirming the intended behavior for the all-projects case and documenting/testing it.

Substring match treats "!event.type:error" as an error-focused query

_is_error_focused_query does a naive substring check `if "event.type:error" in query`. A query like "!event.type:error" (exclude errors) or "(event.type:transaction) AND !event.type:error" also contains that substring, so it returns True. Combined with the allowlist check, count() in such queries will be silently transformed to sum(sample_weight) on the discover dataset even though the query matches non-error events, which either produces wrong counts or breaks because sample_weight doesn't exist for those rows. The query string should be parsed (or at minimum checked for negation) rather than substring-matched.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
fetch_error_details pairs error IDs with nodestore data by zip, assuming matching order

In fetch_error_details, `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict, and the code does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. There is no guarantee that `events.values()` yields entries in the same order as the input `error_ids`/`node_ids` (get_multi returns results keyed by node id, and any missing entries are absent entirely). When ordering differs or an entry is missing, an error ID gets paired with the wrong event's title/message, so the Seer summary will attribute the wrong error text to the wrong event, and timestamps used for chronological interleaving will be wrong. The lookup should be done by node id (e.g. zip(node_ids, error_ids) and use events.get(node_id)).

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TableWidgetVisualization branch renders an empty table, discarding all real data

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reports with neither timestamp nor age pass validation

The BrowserReportSerializer marks both `age` (Working Draft) and `timestamp` (Editor's Draft) as required=False, and the cross-field validators only reject the case where both are present. A report containing neither field is accepted and recorded, even though the Reporting API spec requires one of them and the docstring says 'Validate that age is absent, but timestamp is present' (and vice versa). Additionally, the cross-field checks use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")`), so `age: 0` combined with a timestamp would slip through both validators.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
Error events are merged into every paginated segment page, duplicating error logs

The endpoint paginates recording segments with GenericOffsetPaginator and calls analyze_recording_segments(error_events, segments) per page. get_request_data interleaves the full error_events list into each page's logs (error_idx resets to 0 on every call), so a replay whose segments span multiple pages will have the same 'User experienced an error: ...' log lines repeated once per page in the payload sent to Seer. This inflates and distorts the summary. The error events should either be merged only once (e.g. only on the first page, or filtered to the timestamps covered by the current page's segments).

Flex justify="right" is not a valid justify-content value

The delete-button wrapper was changed to `<Flex justify="right">`. `right` is not a valid CSS justify-content value (valid options include flex-end, center, space-between, etc.), so the justification silently does nothing and the Delete button will not be right-aligned as intended. Use `justify="flex-end"`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing code reuse under concurrency

The code decrypts the backup code list, checks `indexOf`, sets `backupCodes[index] = null`, and re-encrypts in a separate update. Two concurrent login requests presenting the same backup code can both read the list before either writes, both pass the `indexOf` check, and both be authenticated — defeating the single-use guarantee of backup codes (which the UI copy explicitly promises: 'Each backup code can be used exactly once'). The check-and-consume should be made atomic (e.g., a transaction with a conditional update, or a per-code row with a unique consumed marker).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code minLength/maxLength rely on native validation that is disabled on the login form

The input enforces the code length via native `minLength={10}`/`maxLength={11}` attributes, but the login form in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` renders with `noValidate`, so these constraints are never enforced there; any-length string is submitted as `backupCode`. Additionally the placeholder/format 'XXXXX-XXXXX' is 11 characters with the dash, so a correctly formatted code sits at the maxLength boundary and the 10-char minimum rejects a valid 10-char code entered without the dash. Move length/format validation into the zod schema or the server (the server already strips dashes, so client-side length constraints are redundant and currently misleading).

Backup codes cannot be used by Google/SAML users with 2FA, locking them out

In the credentials authorize callback, the guard `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` runs before the new backup-code branch. Users who log in via Google/SAML and have 2FA enabled go through the totp JWT flow (`loginWithTotp`), which submits no totpCode and no password — so if they lose their authenticator and try a backup code, they get 'third-party-identity-provider-enabled' instead of the backup-code check. Backup codes are precisely the recovery mechanism for lost authenticator access, so these users have no recovery path at all. The IdP checks should be skipped when a valid backupCode is supplied (the backup code itself is the second factor).

Consumed backup codes become permanent null entries; once all 10 are used there is no recovery or regeneration path

Used codes are replaced with `null` inside the stored array rather than removed, and there is no endpoint or UI to regenerate backup codes. After all 10 codes are consumed, `user.backupCodes` is still non-null, so the 'MissingBackupCodes' branch never triggers; the user just gets 'incorrect-backup-code' forever. The new locale string 'missing_backup_codes' tells users to 'generate them in your settings', but no such settings UI exists in this PR, so the message directs users to a non-existent feature. Either add a regeneration flow (e.g., rerun setup) or fix the message and prune null entries.

Dismissing the dialog after enabling 2FA (Esc/overlay click) skips onEnable and leaves stale state

After `handleEnable` succeeds, the modal moves to the DisplayBackupCodes step, and `onEnable()` (which notifies the parent that 2FA is now enabled, updating the settings switch) is only called from the explicit 'Close' button. If the user dismisses the dialog via Escape or clicking the overlay, `onOpenChange` fires, `onEnable` is never called, and `resetState` is never run — the parent UI still shows 2FA as disabled even though it is enabled in the database, and reopening the modal resumes at the stale DisplayBackupCodes step. Handle cleanup in `onOpenChange` (or a useEffect on `open`) so enable notification and state reset happen on any close path.

No tests cover the core new behavior: logging in with a backup code or disabling 2FA with one

The PR's main feature is using backup codes during the 2FA login flow and in the disable-2FA flow, but the only test additions exercise the setup screen's copy/download/close buttons, and the file itself adds a TODO admitting login-with-backup and disable-with-backup tests are missing. The single-use consumption logic in the credentials provider, the dash-stripping (`replaceAll('-', '')`), and the new error paths (IncorrectBackupCode, MissingBackupCodes) are entirely untested. The PR checklist also states no tests were added proving the feature works. At minimum, an e2e test should log in with a backup code and verify the same code is rejected on a second attempt.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback find() can never match, producing undefined calendarId

In both `updateEvent` (line ~254-256) and `deleteEvent` (line ~315-317), the fallback branch is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This branch is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined), so `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never be true and the expression always evaluates to `undefined`. Previously the fallback used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which resolved to the destination calendar. Now, when `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` are called without an explicit external calendar id, `calendarId` becomes `undefined` (update) and the Google API call will fail or target the wrong calendar. false_positives.candidate:
Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet

In `EventManager.create()`, the code destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then immediately accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When an event has Google Meet (`MeetLocationType`) as its location but no destination calendar (empty array or null — which this PR now produces in many places, e.g. handleNewBooking sets `null` and other handlers set `[]`), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and reading `.integration` throws a TypeError, breaking booking creation. In `createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is computed via `destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and falls back to `"primary"` only for the `events.insert` call. The follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that writes the hangout link description uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly, without the `"primary"` fallback. Recurring-event cancellation deletes are re-executed once per calendar reference

The recurring-event deletion block (`if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings)`) iterates over all of the user's calendar credentials and all updated bookings. This PR wrapped that block inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`, so with multiple calendar references (now normal for multi-host collective bookings) the same full sweep of deletes runs once per reference — deleting the same events N times and pushing duplicate promises into `apiDeletes`. For collective events, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on `null`. So if the main host has no destination calendar but other collective hosts do, those hosts' calendars are never added and they won't get calendar events — the exact scenario this PR is meant to fix. The code should initialize an array first (e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` before pushing, or use `(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []).concat(teamDestinationCalendars)`).

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token" and persisted

When the parsed response has no refresh_token, the code sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Callers (e.g. zoom, which merges parsedToken.data over the stored key) then write this placeholder into the credential in the DB, destroying the real refresh token and permanently breaking subsequent refreshes for that credential. If the provider omits a refresh token, the existing stored one should be preserved instead of a sentinel string.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

In refreshAccessToken, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` returns a zod SafeParseReturnType ({ success, data }), and that whole object is then written to the DB via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously the code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the parsed token). After this change the credential key becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` instead of the token payload, so the next time the credential is loaded `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the Google Calendar integration breaks for every user whose token is refreshed. The fix is to use `key.data` (after checking success) as the value stored.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

With syncing enabled, the self-hoster's sync endpoint receives a credential id where it expects a Cal.com user id, so token refreshes for zoho-bigin will look up the wrong user (or fail) and return tokens for the wrong account.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Salesforce CalendarService uses prisma without importing it

The newly added block in getClient calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)` but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";` (check the import list — only jsforce, rrule, zod, calcom libs, types, getAppKeysFromSlug and parseRefreshTokenResponse are imported). Salesforce token is refreshed on every client construction regardless of expiry

Every calendar operation (create/update/delete, and availability flows that construct services) now incurs an extra Salesforce auth round-trip plus a credential write, slowing requests and burning through Salesforce's refresh-token rotation / rate limits unnecessarily. Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time !== on a raw header value

The endpoint authenticates by comparing `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` with a plain string inequality. This is a timing-attackable comparison on a secret that guards writing arbitrary OAuth credentials for any userId. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers).

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

Duplicate/blacklist checks are case-sensitive and racy, allowing duplicate attendees

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin OR owner check uses && instead of ||

`isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, so it is only true when the caller is both an admin AND an owner of the team. A team admin who is not the owner (or an owner who is not flagged admin) will be rejected with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to a team booking, even though the UI offers them the action. true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Any existing attendee can add arbitrary guests and trigger organizer-branded emails/calendar updates

The authorization check allows any existing attendee of the booking (`isAttendee`) to add new guests. An attendee can therefore add unlimited arbitrary email addresses (the schema has no upper bound on the `guests` array), which causes calendar invitations and 'AttendeeScheduledEmail' emails to be sent from the organizer's identity/calendar to anyone the attendee chooses. Additionally, when an attendee performs the action, `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and the `EventManager` are built from the attendee's credentials rather than the organizer's, so `updateCalendarAttendees` either fails or operates on the wrong user's calendar. This should likely be restricted to the organizer/team admins, and credentials should come from the booking organizer.

Email failures swallowed with console.log and no error detail

The try/catch around `sendAddGuestsEmails` logs only the static string "Error sending AddGuestsEmails" and drops the actual error, and it runs after `updateCalendarAttendees`, which is unguarded. New addGuests mutation has no tests

The PR adds a new authenticated mutation that mutates booking attendees, updates external calendars, and sends emails, with non-trivial authorization logic (organizer / team admin-owner / attendee), but includes no unit or integration tests. The broken `&&` in the admin/owner check is exactly the kind of defect a permission test would have caught.

No status check allows adding guests to cancelled/rejected/past bookings

The handler fetches the booking without filtering on `status` and never verifies the booking is ACCEPTED/upcoming. Guests can be added to a cancelled or rejected booking, and the emails/ICS sent by `sendAddGuestsEmails` are generated with `status: "CONFIRMED"`, so recipients receive a confirmed calendar invitation for a cancelled event.

No upper bound on guests array enables mass invitation/email abuse

`guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`, so a single authenticated request can add hundreds of attendees to a booking, each generating calendar invites and emails sent from the organizer's address. Add a reasonable maximum (e.g. `.max(10)`) consistent with the booking flow's guest limits.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount increment is a read-modify-write race, not atomic

Both the `else` branch (line 184) and the `catch` block (line 195) compute `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched earlier in `findMany`. If two cron invocations overlap (this endpoint is triggered by an external cron and processing a large batch can exceed the cron interval), both runs read the same retryCount and write the same value, losing an increment. More importantly, if the row was already updated by a concurrent run, the stale value overwrites it. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` so concurrent runs cannot clobber each other's counts.

false_positives.candidate:
Retry-based deletion silently drops reminders that failed for transient reasons

The `deleteMany` with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` deletes any reminder that failed scheduling twice, regardless of why. Failures counted include transient infrastructure problems (Twilio outage, DB errors thrown inside the try, e.g. the `prisma.profile.findFirst` lookup) since the catch block increments retryCount for any error, not just SMS provider rejections like invalid phone numbers. After two transient failures the reminder is permanently deleted and the attendee/host never receives the SMS, with no notification or logging of the deletion. Consider only incrementing for known-permanent provider errors, or at least logging deleted reminder IDs.

retryCount update in catch block can throw and abort the entire cron run

The `catch` block performs an unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update`. If the original error was a database connectivity failure (a plausible cause of scheduling errors), this update will also fail, and since nothing catches it the exception propagates out of the `for` loop, aborting processing of all remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch and returning a 500. UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId on selected calendars, breaking other callers
